case_facts_html:
Beloved Finance Ltd. is a financial enterprise which is in the business of lending loan to small businesses and earn interest on loans. During the year the Company has lend 50 crores and earned ₹1.5 crore as interest on loans. The Company had surplus funds during the year and invested then in Fixed Deposits with bank and earned interest on fixed deposits of ₹20 lacs. The Company also acquired a gold loan unit for ₹10 crore during the year and the Company provided interest free loan of ₹15 crore to its wholly-owned subsidiary. The Company paid a total income tax of ₹75 lacs for the year.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions.
question_html: In the Cash Flow Statement as per AS 3, the interest income of ₹1.5 crore earned on loans given by the Company will be disclosed as:
answer_html: Answer: (A) Operating Activities — for a financial enterprise (whose principal revenue-generating activity is lending), interest received on loans made in the ordinary course of business is classified as an operating cash flow, not an investing one.
topic_text: AS 3 (2.4): Interest received by a financial enterprise on its core lending activity is an operating cash flow

case_facts_html:
Axis limited is a manufacturing company. It purchased a machinery costing ₹10 Lakhs in April 2023. It paid ₹4 lakhs upfront and paid the remaining ₹6,00,000 as deferred payment by paying instalment of ₹1,05,000 for the next 6 months. During the year, the Company sold a land which was classified as its ‘property, plant and equipment’ for ₹25,00,000 and paid ₹1,00,000 as income tax as long term capital gain on such sale. During the year, the Company also received income tax refund along with interest.

Answer the following questions based on the above information.
question_html: As per the requirements of AS 3, ‘Cash Flow Statements’, how the amount for purchase of machinery should be presented:

options.A: ₹10 lakhs as ‘Cash flows from Investing Activities’ and ₹30,000 will simply be booked in profit and loss with no presentation in Cash Flow Statement.
options.B: ₹10.30 lakhs as ‘Cash flows from Investing Activities’ as entire amount is spend on purchase of machinery.
options.C: ₹10 lakhs as ‘Cash flows from Investing Activities’ and ₹30,000 as ‘Cash flows from Financing Activities’.
options.D: ₹10.30 lakhs as ‘Cash flows from Financing Activities’ as the machinery has been purchased on finance.

answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹10 lakhs as Investing Activities and ₹30,000 as Financing Activities — the cash price of ₹10 lakhs is the investing outflow for acquiring the fixed asset; the extra ₹30,000 paid under the deferred-instalment terms (6 × ₹1,05,000 = ₹6,30,000 vs. ₹6,00,000 cash-price-equivalent of the deferred portion) is a finance charge, classified as a financing activity, not part of the investing outflow.
topic_text: AS 3 (2.3): Deferred-credit asset purchase split between investing (cash price) and financing (interest element)

Assets: PPE ₹23,00,000; Goodwill ₹8,00,000; Inventories ₹5,00,000; Trade Receivables ₹2,00,000; Cash & Cash Equivalents ₹2,00,000.

Due to an accumulated debit balance in P&L, a reconstruction scheme was approved (special resolution, NCLT approval, creditors notified), executed 1st April, 2025: (i) equity shares reduced from ₹10 to ₹6 per share, fully paid; (ii) 9% redeemable preference shares reduced to ₹70 fully paid; (iii) the balance created in Capital Reduction account was utilized to completely write off the accumulated P&L debit balance, and the remaining balance used to write off goodwill.

As on 31st March, 2026 (post-reconstruction): (1) PBT for 2025-26 was ₹12,00,000; (2) after charging depreciation of ₹2,00,000 on PPE; (3) trade receivables increased by ₹1,00,000, inventories/trade payables/other liabilities unchanged; (4) Income tax paid ₹3,00,000 during the year.

On 1st April, 2026 (fully executed same day): (i) redeem the entire outstanding 9% Redeemable Preference Shares at a premium of 5%; (ii) buy back 40,000 Equity shares at ₹9 per share. Both redemption and buy-back carried out entirely out of free reserves (General reserve and Current year Profit).
